newsitem.title: USA: Boeing gets two orders for business jets.
newsitem.headline: Boeing gets two orders for business jets.

text.p: Boeing Co has received two new orders for its business jets, giving it a total of 20 orders.
Boeing said in a statement Saturday that the customers have asked to remain anonymous.
The business jet is a high-performance derivative of the Boeing 737-700 with a range of 7,140 statute miles (11,480 km) and a cruising speed of 550 miles per hour, Boeing said.
The engines are produced by CFM International, a 50/50 joint company of General Electric Co and SNECMA of France, Boeing said.
Boeing Business Jets is a joint venture of Boeing and General Electric.
The price for an unfurnished airplane is $30.5 million, but that price will rise to $32 million on July 1, 1997.
A completely furnished and equipped business jet will cost approximately $40 million for delivery in late 1999.
The first Boeing Business Jet is scheduled to roll out in June 1998, Boeing said. General Electric will take delivery of the first Boeing Business Jet in autumn 1998.
